record.paper_title: Open problems posed at the tenth International conference on fuzzy set theory and applications (FSTA 2010, Liptovsky Jan, Slovakia)
record.original_question: For an integer n at least 3, characterize or represent the n-ary copulas C:[0,1]^n -> [0,1] that are associative in Post's sense: for all x1, ..., x_{2n-1} in [0,1], all ways of applying C to one consecutive block of n inputs and then applying C to the resulting n inputs give the same value. The goal is a structural representation for n-ary associative copulas analogous in purpose to the known classification of binary associative copulas.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A function $C:[0,1]^n\to[0,1]$ (with $n\ge 2$) is called an $n$-ary copula if it is grounded (equal to $0$ whenever some argument is $0$), has $1$ as a neutral element in each coordinate (i.e. $C(1,\dots,1,x,1,\dots,1)=x$), and is $n$-increasing in the sense that for every $n$-box $\prod_{i=1}^n[a_i,b_i]\subseteq[0,1]^n$ the associated $C$-volume is nonnegative. Such a $C$ is said to be associative in the sense of Post if for every integer $n\ge 3$ and all $x_1,\dots,x_{2n-1}\in[0,1]$,
$$C\bigl(C(x_1,\dots,x_n),x_{n+1},\dots,x_{2n-1}\bigr)=C\bigl(x_1,C(x_2,\dots,x_{n+1}),x_{n+2},\dots,x_{2n-1}\bigr)=\cdots=C\bigl(x_1,\dots,x_{n-1},C(x_n,\dots,x_{2n-1})\bigr),$$
i.e. all ways of applying $C$ to a single consecutive block of $n$ of the $2n-1$ inputs and then applying $C$ to the resulting $n$ values yield the same number.

For a fixed integer $n\ge 3$, give a structural characterization (representation theorem) of all $n$-ary copulas $C:[0,1]^n\to[0,1]$ that are associative in the sense of Post, analogous to the Ling-type Archimedean/ordinal-sum classification of binary associative copulas.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2011 paper by Stupňanová and Kolesárová in Kybernetika ("Associative n-dimensional copulas") addresses this problem, showing that Post-associative n-ary copulas are essentially n-ary extensions of associative 2-dimensional copulas with additional constraints, and provides a generator-based representation for those satisfying a diagonal inequality. This is presented as a solution/major progress on the open problem, though full structural classification (e.g. ordinal-sum analogues) in all generality may not be complete.

status_evidence.title: Associative n-dimensional copulas
status_evidence.snippet: The associativity of n-dimensional copulas in the sense of Post is studied. These copulas are shown to be just n-ary extensions of associative 2-dimensional copulas with special constraints.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is addressed and largely answered by reducing Post-associative n-copulas to suitably constrained associative binary copulas, with a generator representation in the Archimedean case.
